newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's Ujpest plans soccer flotation.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's Ujpest plans soccer flotation.

text.p: Hungarian soccer club Ujpest plans to become the first club in eastern Europe to seek a stock market flotation by listing its shares on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE).
Club president, former Olympic fencing champion Bence Szabo, 35, said he plans a radical overhaul of the club's structure to attract foreign investment.
"Football is no longer just a sport," Szabo told Reuters. "It has become part of the entertainment business."
Ujpest is part of a larger sports club with 15 sections including water-polo and fencing. The 70-member executive will meet on Monday to vote on separating out the football activities.
Szabo would not be drawn on whether Ujpest would sell a majority share in the initial public offering, which is another sign of the increasing role private investors are taking in Hungarian football.
Two years ago, current champions MTK were bought by a Hungarian company Sportinvest, owned by Hungarian Gabor Varszegi, CEO of consumer goods retailer Fotex.

Brian Sturgess, of ING Barings in London, a media analyst who specialises in football stocks, welcomed Ujpest's plans. He said Ujpest would clearly attract interest from local investors but also needed to draw institutional investors.
Ujpest, known as Ujpest Dozsa during the communist era, when they were backed by Hungary's Interior Ministry, is one of Hungary's most successful clubs.
